### y2v3 p.72–74 — Night: solitude and Tsukishiro’s playbook
[scene] (p.72) Total darkness; insects; running through grass; camping alone = battle against solitude; the harshest part — Tsukishiro will certainly try to have him expelled.
[trait] (p.73) Notes lone girls like Horikita or Ibuki face brutal toilet improvisation; he holds his breath in the tent.
[scene] (p.73–74) Analysis: head-on expulsion impossible (students control their own points); most probable angle: force retirement through injury (White Room enforcer; broken arm; “accident” deep in the forest; GPS complaint risk means Mashima/the school would scent something if the number of missed days is small). An indirect approach is likelier and more dangerous.
[goal] (p.73–74) Anticipate Tsukishiro’s indirect route: tampered watch/tablet (too traceable), or a staged injury in the unpatrolled forest to force his retirement.

### y2v3 p.79–81 — Nanase asks to tag along
[scene] (p.79) She doesn't leave after the greeting; she pauses, asks for the favor of accompaniment.
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.79) “Um, Ayanokōji-senpai, there’s a favor I’d like to ask of you.”
[says] (p.79) “A favor?”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.79) “If it’s not too much trouble, would you perhaps allow me to accompany you for a while?”
[says] (p.79) “Accompany me? What do you mean by that?”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.79) “To tell you the truth, a slight issue came up as my group was talking last night. Both Hōsen-kun and Amasawa-san felt that we would be better off if we all acted independently, so everything more or less fell apart.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.80) “I’ve crossed paths with you a total of three times now, Senpai. From what I’ve seen from our encounters, I believe that you’ve managed to reach the designated area faster than me. That is of course, except for the first time. I fear that if I’m on my own, it won’t be long before I start to fall behind the designated areas.”
[says] (p.80) “Don’t you think it’s possible that I just happened to be faster than you these last two times?”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.80) “That may be so indeed, but either way, I’ve still recognized you as a step above someone as inexperienced as myself.”
[says] (p.80) “I don’t think it’s a very wise idea to travel together with someone in a different school year.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.80) “You’re saying that due to the influence it would have on Early Bird Bonuses and the increased competition for Tasks, correct?”
[says] (p.80) “There would be a conflict of interest if we came across a Task that only had room for one more group.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.80) “I would be perfectly fine with taking the back seat in that regard, Ayanokōji-senpai. I would only step foot into the designated area after you’ve checked to make sure you’ve received your points and Bonuses. That way, it shouldn’t place you at a disadvantage. As for Tasks, I’ll just defer to you should there only be one space remaining.”
[says] (p.80) “You’d ultimately lose points by doing that, Nanase.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.80) “This is my first uninhabited island exam, and you’ve already proven the extent of your physical abilities during your fight with Hōsen-kun. It would be immensely helpful to me if I could have you choose a suitable route for us to take.”
[says] (p.81) “Even if we assume that I’m going to choose the most suitable route, would you be able to keep pace with me? Sometimes the path I choose might even be dangerous. Would you really be able to do it?”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.81) “I’m fairly confident in my stamina. …You’re not uncertain because you think I might hold you back, it’s more that you’re not able to trust me, isn’t it?”
[says] (p.81) “Alright. If that’s what you want, then go ahead.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.81) “Thank you very much.”
[note] (p.81) Her answer only names his distrust; both sides understand the stalker-or-saved question; a tail is worse than a companion if their Tables match — he folds on the low-cost option.

### y2v3 p.234–242 — Sakayanagi; Mashima-sensei; two boats
[scene] (p.234–239) He finds Sakayanagi seated under a parasol with Ichinose and Shibata nearby; the Early Bird exception; the plan pitch; her counter-negotiation (“if you’re willing to stomach working with me under the same conditions”); the timetable warning.

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.234) “The school has graciously decided to make an exception for my group. After all, it’s not my fault that I’m forced to stay sedentary.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.234) “I must ask, what brings you to the starting area today?”
[says] (p.234) “There were a few reasons, but the first didn’t play out according to plan.”
[says] (p.234) “Unfortunately, the final spot was taken by Kōenji.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.234) “He was in fourth place just this morning, and yet now he’s already in second? As a classmate of yours, he’s quite the prodigy, isn’t he?”
[says] (p.234) “I hold the same opinion.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.234) “It should be about half an hour until the Task is over and Nanase-san comes back, so you’re welcome to come join me if you’d like. The shade here is wonderfully refreshing, I must say.”

[says] (p.236) “How do you know about Nanase?”

[says] (p.236) “Are you sure it’s okay for me to join you? I’m an enemy after all.”
[says] (p.238) “Actually, there’s a favor I’d like to ask of you, Sakayanagi.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “Ayanokōji-kun himself is asking me? Well now isn’t that intriguing? Please, do go on.”
[says] (p.238) “Five days have passed since the exam started, and yet only two people have retired.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “Komiya-kun and Kinoshita-san, right? It seems you’re fairly well informed yourself.”
[says] (p.238) “Incidentally, I just happened to be there when they retired.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “From what I’ve gathered by looking at the rankings, the remaining Shinohara-san still seems to be putting forth the effort to stay afloat… As such, I would reckon that she’s working with someone else now in order to get through the rest of the exam, is that right?”
[says] (p.238) “Correct.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “Though, given her abilities, it would be considerably difficult for her to navigate the second half of the battle on her own. Ideally, she should look to get absorbed by some other group sooner rather than later… Ah, I see what you’re after.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “So you want to get me to cooperate? Have you already met with Ryūen-kun?”
[says] (p.238) “He’s on board with my plan. It seems he thinks quite highly of Komiya and Kinoshita.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.238) “Is that so?”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.239) “It’s only natural that Ryūen-kun would lend a hand given the circumstances, but I don’t see any merit in doing so myself. At some level, I suppose that it would be prudent to prevent second-year Class Points from falling into the hands of the other school years. But to be honest, if there’s no harm done to Class 2-A, I don’t think it warrants any kind of intervention on my part.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.239) “But, if you’re willing to stomach working with me under the same conditions, I wouldn’t be opposed to helping you out.”
[says] (p.239) “I’d like to agree to your condition, but I lack the necessary manpower right now.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.239) “I’ll gladly wait for when you’re ready, of course. This strategy of yours will require both time and effort to execute, so if you want to take action, it’d be best to do so sooner rather than later.”
[says] (p.239) “I’ll contact you later.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.239) “I’ll leave it to you to decide on a messenger then. Whether it be Horikita-san or Ryūen-kun, it’s of no concern to me.”
[scene] (p.240–241) Mashima-sensei at the provisions desk; the two boats intel; the tent where Tsukishiro watches; his patrol; the bad feeling; the warning.
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.240) “Ah, Ayanokōji. Perfect timing actually. I have something to tell you, so make it seem like you’re looking through the merchandise and listen up.”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.240) “Acting Director Tsukishiro hasn’t done anything noteworthy so far, at least not since the exam started. I haven’t noticed him planning anything to interfere with you.”
[says] (p.240) “So you’re saying I don’t need to worry about him doing anything?”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.240) “…That’s what I’d like to tell you, but there are still certain things that seem a bit strange.”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.240) “In this exam, there’s no telling when or where someone might run into danger. In the event that a student suffers a particularly time-critical injury, the school has prepared a small boat and a helicopter to help expedite the rescue process.”
[says] (p.240) “That seems reasonable to me.”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.240) “We originally planned on bringing along one helicopter and one boat… found that the Acting Director had arranged it as a supposed safety precaution.”
[says] (p.241) “So then, maybe it’s possible that he did so expecting the need for two boats to arise at once?”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.241) “That’s certainly true. In the end, it’s just something peculiar that I thought would be worth mentioning. Take it for what you will.”
[says] (p.241) “Where does the Acting Director usually spend his time?”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.241) “Generally, he stays in the tent where the monitoring equipment has been set up, making sure that nothing has gone wrong with any of the students’ watches. Of course, other staff members are in there monitoring the watches as well. Outside of that, he tends to go out and patrol the island once or twice a day, sometimes for several hours at a time.”
[says] (p.241) “The Acting Director goes out of his way to patrol the island, all on his own?”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.241) “Yes.”
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.241) “In any case, I have a bad feeling about all of this, so be sure to watch your back, Ayanokōji.”
[says] (p.241) “Thank you for going to the trouble of providing me with this warning.”
### y2v3 p.242–250 — Onodera wins; B6; the bottom-ten complacency think
[scene] (p.242–244) Nanase finishes the swim — third place; Onodera of Class 2-D wins; Kōenji swims past all in record time; B6 random designation; the bottom-ten complacency/expulsion logic; the long walk through forest.

[says] (p.244) “It’ll be hard if we try to go straight through the forest. However, we can take the beach in D8 and C8 and cut through a shorter patch of forest to the beach in B8 instead. Then, if we just head north from there, we can get to B6 without too much trouble.”
[scene] (p.245–249) The forest; thirst; the analysis of thatbany's comfort logic; the real resolve lecture; her Emilie analysis; he shares a little of his plan; Nanase silent and attentive; the enemy vs enemy question.
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.245) “There are more groups huddled around the starting area than I expected. I wonder if that’s due to the stress and difficulty that comes with living on the island for four or five days in a row? What do you think, Senpai?”
[says] (p.245) “I think that’s part of it, but that’s not the only reason. I’d say the largest factor is the revelation of the bottom ten groups.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.245) “…Is that so? Well, the expulsion penalty only applies to the bottom five groups, and since they were given the ability to find out their current situation through their tablets on the fourth day, I suppose it makes sense that they’ve grown complacent…”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.246) “But, even if you have a 10 to 20 point lead on the bottom five, there’s no absolute guarantee that you’ll be safe, right? If it were me, I’d try my best to establish a 30 to 40 point lead and work to maintain it.”
[says] (p.246) “Of course, at some level, everyone knows that they should be doing it that way. After all, everyone wants to face the special exam with the resolve to give it their all from start to finish. But reality is not that kind. Just like how you and I are eager to get a drink of water right now, once you get a taste of something sweet, whatever resolve you might have is bound to falter.”
[says] (p.247) “Rest is important. There are times where you’ll have no choice but to overwork yourself to earn points, but the key to that is knowing when to push yourself and when to take a step back and take a break. You ultimately just have to avoid doing the same things as the majority of other students.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.247) “I’ve been thinking that you’ve been taking on the exam fairly negligently these past few days, Ayanokōji-senpai. But, you’ve just been conducting yourself that way because you don’t want to stand out too much during the first half, haven’t you?”
[says] (p.247) “That’s about right. Of course, I’ll bite if an adequate opportunity presents itself, but even if I made it into a highly contested Task, the number of points I can earn would be limited.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.248) “Uhm, if I may ask… why are you telling me about your plan? Up until now, it has always seemed that you’ve been looking to placate or deceive me whenever the topic comes up, Senpai.”
[says] (p.249) “Put simply, there’s no questioning the fact you’re my enemy, Nanase. Not only because this exam requires us to compete against each other as students from different school years, but also because there’s 20 million private points in it for you for getting me expelled.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.249) “…That’s right. After all, I tried to plot against you before, Senpai.”
[says] (p.249) “That being said, your actions so far have made it impossible for me to see you as an enemy.”

[says] (p.256) “…I’m not 100% certain I get what you two are going on about, but I don’t think we should go out with each other.”

[says:andou-sayo] (p.257) “Ooooo, is that modesty I see? You do know that you were quite the hit with the girls back when we first enrolled here, right Ayanokōji-kun?”

[says:minamikata-kozue] (p.258) “Well, ain’t no helpin’ that. There’s no way to tell if you’re gonna like a guy unless you up and talk with ‘em face-to-face, and Ayanokōji-kun wasn’t the type a’ guy to talk with people a year ago.”

[scene] (p.67) Inside the tent: Ibuki Mio sits chewing on jerky — Class 2-B’s class-wide strategy of homemade jerky (fresh meat not prepacked, cheaper than the school’s prices); she’s emaciated, dark circles, hasn’t spoken to anyone but Horikita since day one.
[says] (p.67) “You’re really─ Wait, no, what are you eating?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.67) “Jerky.”
[says] (p.67) “Jerky…? That wasn’t included in the Uninhabited Island Manuel they handed out to us before the exam, though?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.67) “What’s it matter to you? It’s none of your business.”
[says] (p.68) “How many people have you spoken with since the exam started?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.68) “Wha…?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.68) “…Just Horikita. You heard me say I wouldn’t lose to her, right? You were there.”
[says] (p.68) “In other words, you’re saying you haven’t had a proper conversation with someone since day one?”
[says] (p.68) “You should try and find someone to talk to, even if only a little bit.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.68) “Ain’t no way I’m gonna talk with my enemies.”
[says] (p.68) “Then talk with a classmate. If you wander around long enough, you’re sure to come across someone.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.69) “I don’t think of my classmates as ‘friends’.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.69) “Get out already.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.70) “How many points you got right now?”
[says] (p.70) “We’re mutual enemies, you do know that right?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.70) “So you won’t tell me.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.71) “…Whatever. It was a waste of time to bother with askin’ you anyway.”
[says] (p.71) “Fair enough. Besides, your true target here is Horikita, right?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.71) “When you next see that bitch, do me a solid and tell her that I’ll absolutely never lose to her.”
[says] (p.71) “That’s fine and all, but I’m probably not the one you should be giving the middle finger to.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.71) “You, her, same difference. After all, you two are on real good terms with each other.”
[says] (p.71) “Hold on a moment.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.72) “Haaa? You tryna pull somethin’?”
[says] (p.72) “That wasn’t my intention here at all, but─”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.72) “The hell are you doing!?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.72) “I’ll admit I can’t beat you, sure, but one of these days, I swear I’m gonna get the satisfaction of kickin’ your teeth in.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.72) “So? Did Horikita put you up to this? Tryna get in my way?”
[says] (p.72) “Your pulse is racing.”
[says] (p.73) “The inside of your mouth looks dry too, not to mention how cracked your lips are. You’re obviously dehydrated.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.73) “I’m not all that thirsty… anymore.”
[says] (p.73) “Anymore? So then, you’re saying you were thirsty at one point?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.73) “Mind your own business. There ain’t anything wrong with me.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “Wait, wha─? What are you doing!?”
[says] (p.74) “Show me what’s inside.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “Haaa!? No way in hell I’mma show a guy. No, I wouldn’t even do it for a girl either.”
[says] (p.74) “Fair enough.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “Hey! I said no!”
[says] (p.74) “How long have you been out of water?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “I don’t have to tell you anythi─”
[says] (p.74) “I said, how long have you been out of water?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “…A full day… and then some.”
[says] (p.74) “Nope. I’ve been resting here all day today.”
[says] (p.74) “What an obvious lie. There were no GPS signals anywhere near here this morning.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “You did a GPS Search?”
[says] (p.74) “Has your first Warning Alert gone off yet?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.74) “…It did about an hour ago. That’s why I reluctantly decided to turn in early for the night.”
[says] (p.75) “If you don’t rehydrate at some point, it’ll keep ringing even if you rest.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.75) “I’ll handle it tomorrow, and if push comes to shove I’ll even go back to the starting area, so drop it and leave me alone.”
[says] (p.75) “It’s more than two kilometers from here to the starting area. If you were to collapse along the way, it’d be all over.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.75) “Then I’ll just do a nearby Task or some shit.”
[says] (p.75) “You can’t do that though, can you? Otherwise you wouldn’t be in the state you’re in now.”
[says] (p.75) “Trade me.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.75) “What?”
[says] (p.75) “It just so happens that I’m running short on food. On the other hand, I have a bit of an oversupply of water. I’m asking you to negotiate with me since I think we can make a fair trade.”
[says] (p.76) “How about it? I’ll say it again just to be sure, but I’m looking to make a fair trade here. You’ll have to give me a suitable amount of food in exchange.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.76) “Who the hell do you think you are to─”
[says] (p.76) “Feel free to say no, but I won’t be giving you a chance to change your mind.”
[says] (p.76) “If you retire due to dehydration like this, you’ll definitely lose to Horikita. In fact, I met with Horikita a little while ago. Her complexion was perfectly fine, and she didn’t seem to be having any problems with water or food either.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.76) “I get it… I’ll trade with you. But, how much do you want from me?”
[says] (p.76) “Half of your remaining food. That should be enough.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.76) “Only that much?”
[says] (p.76) “It’s at least better than sustaining myself by eating random weeds.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.77) “I’m not gonna thank you if that’s what you’re after. It’s supposed to be a fair trade, remember?”
[says] (p.77) “I don’t want you to thank me.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.77) “Then whatta you want?”
[says] (p.77) “If you’re not doing too badly with points, how about you spend most of the day tomorrow resting? That, or switch to a strategy where you only focus on acquiring food and water?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.77) “So you’re sayin’ for me to give up on scoring points? You’ve gotta be kidding me.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.77) “I’m not puttin’ in all this work ‘cause I don’t wanna get expelled. My only goal here is beating Horikita.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.78) “I’ve got nothin’ more to say to you.”
[trait] (p.66–78) He spots the dehydration pattern instantly (pulse, dry mouth, cracked lips, empty bottle); bluffs a GPS Search to trap her lying about resting; engineers a fair-trade offer using Horikita’s name as the lever — the only thing that moves her; she accepts the trade and walks out.
[rel:ibuki-mio] (p.66–78) She hates him (he’s ‘X’), but she takes the water; he sees her as a lone cannon aimed at Horikita; she bolts without a word.
[rel:horikita-suzune] (p.76) He uses Horikita as leverage — Ibuki’s entire drive is the match against her.

### y2v4 p.79–80 — Ch.3: The backpack rummaged; the 12-point buffer
[scene] (p.79) Next morning she is caught rummaging through his backpack — checking whether the trade was fair; his tablet has a lock screen; he accepts the mistrust as fair retaliation for opening hers.
[says] (p.79) “What are you doing?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.79) “!”
[says] (p.79) “Were you trying to sneak a peek at my tablet, or was there something else you wanted?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.79) “I wouldn’t do somethin’ like that! I just… I just wanted to make sure our trade was actually fair, that’s all.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.79) “You’ve only got one bottle of water left in there, and you’ve already drunk some of it! I thought you said you had too much water?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.79) “So what, were you trying to help me out to get me to owe you a favor?”
[note] (p.79) “Grr…” — he privately notes her cheek twitched at his words.
[says] (p.80) “In other words, I’m telling you that the truth doesn’t matter. It was a fair trade either way.”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.80) “I ain’t convinced, but… I get it. If that’s the way it is, I’m not gonna give any water back to you.”
[says] (p.80) “If I did this to have you owe me a favor, would you pay it back?”
[says:ibuki-mio] (p.80) “No way.”
[says] (p.80) “…Is that so?”
[note] (p.80) At 7:00 AM he spends one point on a GPS Search; Kuronaga is close to him; the one-point spend widens their gap to 12 points — even a first-place Early Bird Bonus keeps him just outside the top ten. Three other groups could contest the bonus; he yields; his first trip to that bonus pool is to save stamina.
[trait] (p.79–80) He lets her win the argument about the trade but notes she can’t bear to owe him; her distrust is mutual.

### y2v4 p.81–85 — Ch.3: Kiryūin Fuka sizes him up
[scene] (p.81) A designated-area arrival; he arrives late and catches Fuka Kiryūin at the overlook; she’s just jumped from 11th or lower to 9th this morning; she debriefs him on the field.
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.81) “You have arrived quite late, Ayanokouji.”
[says] (p.81) “It looks like it is”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.81) “I thought I had a tough competitor for the reward in order of arrival, but was it you?”
[says] (p.81) “I don’t know what’s up with that. It’s not uncommon for there to be different tables in the same area. More than that, I thought that Kiryuuin-senpai was not interested in the top ten groups.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “This uninhabited island test was more fun than I thought it would be, and I was thrilled beyond my age.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “I’m going to continue with my current rhythm for a while longer.”
[says] (p.83) “Shouldn’t you be aiming for number one?”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “Everyone is competing with each other for the podium. I could not continue with that game. However, if Miyabi Nagumo collapses down, the story could be a little different.”
[says] (p.83) “In such a state of conflict and struggle, Nor can I say that Nagumo will ever win. Sure you have been watching everything up to now, but the time has come for you to move your chips. Depending on how things go, we could see a period where neither team scores.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “Because hitting your opponent is an important part of a battle.”
[says] (p.83) “Don’t you aspire to move to the top?”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “I’m sorry, but I don’t see how can I be in the top ten.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.83) “I see. I thought you would have scored almost as many points as I did.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “Several groups will soon lose their performance. We just have to keep trying and not give up.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “That said, from what I see in the table so far, what do you think of the fact that no group has withdrawn?”
[says] (p.84) “All I can say is that you can’t let your guard down, not even for a moment.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “Yesterday I went through the starting point to obtain information. It seems that groups that have started to suffer from food and water shortages are trying to get ahead by separating some of their members to avoid joint collapse.”
[says] (p.84) “It is a wise decision.”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “I am sure that the last 10 will have some hope, no matter which group will withdraw. A man who has lost his way will use whatever means at his disposal. Stay alert, okay?”
[says] (p.84) “Shouldn’t it be something a woman, Kiryuuin-senpai, should be worried about?”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “Hmm… It’s true that, as a pretty and merciful maiden, I might also feel a sense of danger”
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.84) “Well if it comes to that ......., I would just have to force it out.”
[note] (p.85) At this time, he believes there are at most two pools of openings for the challenge; if there are more than three rival groups and Kiryūin also goes there, the odds that she participates collapse.
[says:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.85) “So that’s a.... no, I dare you to go there and see for yourself.”
[trait] (p.81–85) He catalogues her as a third-year with an insight beyond the OAA — she already reads the three-way Kōenji/Nagumo stalemate from the leaderboard and almost tells him too much about his own strategy; he demurs to stay out of her range.
[rel:kiryuin-fuuka] (p.81–85) She is drawn to him (why she keeps pace for the score in a two-stop race) and leaves him with a gambit of her own; he notes her cards are as visible as his.
[rel:nagumo-miyabi] (p.83–84) Both expect the Kōenji–Nagumo deadlock to shatter at some point.

### y2v4 p.86–94 — Ch.3: The Shiranami night search; the walkie-talkie
[scene] (p.86) After nine at night he hears an unstable flashlight beam wandering the forest and a faint voice calling for “Yume” — Shiranami Chihiro, crying; he triangulates: only one Yume in the school, Kobashi of Class 2-C — so the searcher is a classmate.
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.86) “Um, Ayanokouji-kun ...... good night.”
[says] (p.87) “It is quite dangerous to go out alone in the middle of the night. What happened to Kobashi and Takemoto?”

[says] (p.87) “There are a lot of bugs. You may want to get into the tent first.”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.87) “Eh!?”

[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.88) “I'm sorry ...... I was just resting and ....”

[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.88) “Yes.”
[says] (p.88) “Is there a plan in case someone gets lost?”
[says] (p.88) “Is the group still a small group of three? Or is it growing to more than four?”
[says] (p.88) “Very good. You don't have to tell me the details of the situation. Just listen to what I have to say.”
[says] (p.88) “If I were a member of your group, I would be aware of the current situation. I would have concluded that my companion was wandering alone through the dark forest without being able to return.”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.88) “... I don't know ... I think we would go look for Yume-chan ...”
[says] (p.88) “Even if it causes an additional disaster and they risk getting injured and retiring?”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.88) “I couldn't leave her because she's my friend.”
[says] (p.89) “Can you pay points? If you use it 2 times, would you be concerned about your rating after using it three times?”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.89) “That's ... I wonder. I don't think it's good.”
[says] (p.90) “How strong are you?”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.90) “What?”
[says] (p.90) “Do you have the strength to walk?”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.90) “Uh-huh. Okay, but......”
[says] (p.90) “Let's move so we can unite from now on”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.90) “But how?”
[says] (p.90) “It is not a problem that can be solved by walking in the dark. We will use this.”
[says] (p.90) “We can use the GPS search to determine where we are going and the approximate distance travelled.”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.90) “But why….are you going out your way to help me......?”
[says] (p.90) “Why? Since this exam is a battle based on the same year, that's one aspect of it.”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.90) “But even using a GPS search is...”
[says] (p.90) “If I must say. Maybe it's because you're in Ichinose's class.”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.91) “…Maybe...”
[says] (p.91) “Hmm?”
[says:shiranami-chihiro] (p.91) “…Maybe it's because Ayanokouji-kun ... and Honami-chan ..”
[says:kobashi-yume] (p.93) “Thank you, Ayanokouji-kun, for helping Chihiro-chan”
[says] (p.93) “No, I think you would have found her eventually, it wasn't a big deal.”

[says] (p.93) “I have something to ask, do you have a walkie-talkie?”

[says] (p.94) “I just want to talk to her in private.”

[note] (p.93–94) He asks Takemoto to call Sakayanagi: whether any Class D students she dealt with have returned to the starting area; the confession on Takak—it's an exchange about Sakayanagi's Class D dealings; she hands him the walkie-talkie via Takemoto, effectively a gift to him; he sleeps to stories of Classes A and C around him.
[trait] (p.86–94) He walks Shiranami back in the dark with GPS searches; gets their gratitude without revealing his own stake; the Sakayanagi back-channel — Takemoto hands him the walkie-talkie Sakayanagi arranged.
[rel:shiranami-chihiro] (p.86–94) He walks her home through the dark; she owes him; she suspects the Honami-chan connection.
[rel:kobashi-yume] (p.93–94) The lost girl; her companions came searching; he thanks them for the find.
[rel:takemoto-shigeru] (p.93–94) Loan of the walkie-talkie; the relay into Sakayanagi’s channel.
[rel:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.93–94) The back-channel: he asks via Takemoto about Class D dropouts; Sakayanagi answers and hands him her walkie-talkie.

### y2v4 p.116–118 — Ch.4: The six-member group at the sunset
[scene] (p.116) At J10 just before 5:00 p.m., he barely makes the last zone and spots the merged group — three girls from Class 2-B and three more from another sophomore group (Ishizaki Daichi, Takeko Nishino, Hitomi Tsutsube); only Hiyori notices him first and waves.
[says:shiina-hiyori] (p.116) “What? Isn't it Ayanokouji-kun?”

[says:shiina-hiyori] (p.116) “Everyone has worked very hard. We have expanded our group to a maximum of six people.”
[says:shiina-hiyori] (p.118) “That's right. We have several priorities for the merger, and this is one of those groups.”
[says:shiina-hiyori] (p.118) “Ayanokouji-kun, how do you feel?”
[says] (p.118) “Yes. So far, so good.”
[says:shiina-hiyori] (p.118) “I don't think there is anything to worry about, but you have to be careful.”

[says] (p.118) “That's how it is.”

[rel:ishizaki-daichi] (p.116) His side of the merged group waves from afar.

### y2v4 p.120–122 — Ch.4: 2:30 a.m.; Nanase's warning
[scene] (p.120) During the night at I9, Nanase slips to his tent at 2:30 a.m., frightened — she was working with Hōsen all day; she came straight to him.
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.120) “It's me, Nanase.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.120) “I'm fine; I was in I9 like you. In fact, I even saw you from afar at night, but since I was working with Housen-kun, so I decided to avoid contact.”

[says] (p.120) “A great play? It sure isn't the only thing.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.120) “No, no, let me tell you in order.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.121) “I don't know, but Tsubaki was the main person I spoke to on the walkie-talkie.”
[says] (p.121) “It's good that you told us the date and the details until the last moment.”
[says] (p.121) “Oh no, thanks for that, but that's enough for this uninhabited island exam. If you see a freshman moving around, you don't have to come tell me, and you don't have to help me.”
[says:nanase-tsubasa] (p.122) “Nevertheless...”
[says] (p.122) “Nanase, you have given me enough information. Now you must do what you have to do as one of the group of Housen and Amasawa.”

[trait] (p.120–122) He deduces the first-years' day-12 plan: force his withdrawal at the exam's end; seniors alone targeted; Hōsen feigning cooperation; he cuts Nanase loose so she can protect her cover.

[rel:housen-kazuomi] (p.121) Feigning cooperation; holds the walkie-talkie.
[rel:tsubaki-sakurako] (p.121) The intermediary named on the walkie-talkie.

### y2v5 p.13–16 — Chabashira announces the second-semester events
[scene] (p.13) In homeroom, Chabashira outlines a packed second semester: an October sports festival, a November cultural festival (the school's first), plus midterm/final exams and a school trip.
[trivia] (p.14) Cultural festival: each 2nd-year given 5,000 private points (1st-years 5,500, 3rd-years 4,500) for preparation; 100 class points to 1st–4th place, 50 to 5th–8th, none below; extra funds for student council/club contributions; unused funds confiscated.
[trivia] (p.15) Stall locations cost points (Main Gate 1 = 10,000); only one class per location, conflicts settled by bidding war to the school; stall details kept secret until the day (leaks penalized); outside items allowed with permission.
[trait] (p.13–16) Analyzes the rules — the cultural festival is announced first because preparation must start early; suspects there's more to it than the straightforward rules ("evidence that I've become deeply ingrained in the structure of this school").
[rel:chabashira-sae] (p.13–16) Delivers the briefing; he notes she looks the same as first semester.

### y2v5 p.29–44 — The Unanimous Voting Exam briefing
[scene] (p.29) In homeroom, Chabashira announces a surprise special exam *before* the sports festival — held only for second-years, tomorrow.
[trivia] (p.31–42) The "Unanimous Voting Exam": 5 questions, up to 4 options each; all 39 classmates vote anonymously (60 seconds); not unanimous → 10-minute discussion → revote; 5-hour limit; 90 seconds cumulative overtime penalty = expulsion; 50 class points for clearing, −300 for failing; protection points disabled; phones collected; binding agreements/money exchanges forbidden.
[trivia] (p.36–38) If a vote awards points to "one student," that student is chosen by majority nomination (their own vote removed), then the class votes for/against; a unanimous "against" removes them and picks another; candidates may volunteer.
[inference] (p.32–35) Analyzes the sample questions — 5 class points are worth 9,000 private points over the remaining 18 months, so the 10,000-point instant gain is marginally better, but the "just in case" risk of losing Class A matters more; deliberately votes "for" in the practice rounds to avoid unanimity and teach the class how the exam works (Sudō does the same).
[trait] (p.29–44) Watchful — notes Horikita's growth as a "pillar of support" (calmly reframes risk as benefit, winning class approval), sees Chabashira's hidden sweetness, and realizes the exam's real difficulty is the anonymous vote (people can lie about how they voted) and the impossibility of enforced agreements.
[rel:chabashira-sae] (p.29–44) Delivers the briefing; he notes she must be inwardly pleased with the class.
[rel:horikita-suzune] (p.30–31) Her calming leadership earns the class's approval.

### y2v6 p.30–40 — Ch.1: The Sports Festival rules are announced
[scene] (p.30–33) Chabashira explains the Sports Festival's special rules — the Student Council President's experiment emphasizing individual ability: 9AM–4PM (break 12PM–1PM); everyone starts with 5 points and must enter at least 5 events; 1 point participation prize per event; from the sixth event each entry costs 1 point and pays nothing; a maximum of 10 events; fewer than 5 completed events forfeits all points; unsigned withdrawals cost 2 points; events run in parallel across locations; fundamental competitions (individual, fixed rewards: 1st 5 / 2nd 3 / 3rd 1 + 1 participation) and special competitions (team, at least two people, equal split, higher payouts).
[rule] (p.31) “The Sports Festival has been adjusted to ensure that nobody will get expelled for lack of ability, and nobody will have to suffer any penalty alone.”
[rule] (p.32) Rules: 5 points at start; at least 5 events required; participation prize 1 point; from the 6th event onwards, pay 1 point; participation prize not paid from the 6th event; max 10 events; forfeiture of all points if fewer than 5 events; −2 points for unsigned withdrawal; designated cheering areas required after finishing.
[rule] (p.33–34) Class ranking rewards: first 150 points, second 50, third 0, fourth −150; individual rewards (per year, boys and girls separate): first 2 million private points or a Class Change Ticket (Limited Time), second 1 million, third 500,000; same-place tie splits the private reward with no ticket; ticket usable only during the second semester.
[scene] (p.35–40) Sudō erupts at the Class Change Ticket; Chabashira explains “Limited Time” means a second-semester-only use period; AK calculates that a first-place finish needs at least four more firsts to cover the 150/50 gap and notes one student cannot enter more than 10 events; pre-booking via app from 10PM today (first come, first served; up to three cancels; deadline two days before the festival; auto-assignment if fewer than five booked); club-restriction: no event tied to a club one is or ever was a member of (Hirata cannot enter soccer; Sudō cannot enter basketball).
[number] (p.33) Our class with two people missing gets 380 points of starting points against Ichinose's 400 — a 20-point handicap from the start.

### y2v6 p.162–169 — Ch.3: Amasawa's visit — the golden hair; the White Room (AK POV)
[scene] (p.162–164) Mii-chan goes home; AK starts cleaning his room — more visitors lately; the doorbell rings thrice; he looks through the peephole, refuses; Amasawa calls out loudly so the neighbors can hear; he opens the door; she names both Karuizawa-senpai and Wang-senpai as today's visitors — an information network; she denies bugs; she enters uninvited; she reaches for the pillow and lifts a single strand of sparkling golden hair — “Kei’s.”

### y2v6 p.184–193 — Ch.3: The cafe in Keyaki Mall — Haruka's ultimatum (AK POV)
[scene] (p.184) The three members of the Ayanokouji group were waiting at their seats with three drinks placed out in vain; they randomly picked drinks; Haruka urged them to sit without warmth — dispassionate opening; her gaze directed at neither him nor Horikita; then: “In a way, the problem has already been solved.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.184) “Sit down.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.184) “While I was away, you seemed to have wanted to talk to me several times, so I thought I’d ask about that.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.184) “What did you want to talk about?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.184) “In a way, the problem has already been solved. You’d been absent from school for several days.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.184) “So you were worried. Our class evaluation may drop, after all.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.184) “Of course that’s not everything. You must have had a good reason for being absent for a week, right?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.184) “I wasn’t feeling well. I told that to the school, so there shouldn’t be any problems? Miyacchi told me that we may receive a penalty if I’m out more than a week, so I came to school today.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.185) “Certainly. However, the reason you skipped school wasn’t because you weren’t feeling good.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.185) “How can you say that’s the case? I could simply have been sick, right?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.185) “You seem to have your doubts, but I really wasn’t feeling well. It wasn’t an injury or sickness though. Waking up was emotionally difficult, I couldn’t sleep, and simply took off from school.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.185) “Could you stop beating around the bush and say what you want to say?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.185) “Are you satisfied that you gained class points during the special exam?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.185) “I’m not satisfied. There’s still a gap of more than 500 points between us and Class A. Moreover, striving for Class A without losing anyone if possible was my ideal… my vision. However, talking about those things is meaningless at this point.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “My dear friend was sacrificed due to your selfish judgment. Are you aware of that, Horikita-san?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.186) “Indeed.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “What a fine leader. You don’t question the methods you take in order to make your class win.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.186) “I still have ways to go.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “Do you understand that I was being sarcastic?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.186) “Of course I understand.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “Where did your original promise to cut off the traitor – the student who kept pressing “agree” – go?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.186) “Regarding that, I think my foresight was inadequate. However, so long as we can’t make it as if the special exam from the other day never happened, we have no choice but to keep living on.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “There are mistakes that can’t be forgiven.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.186) “I won’t deny that. It’s as you say.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.186) “Even if having Kyou-cha– Kushida-san remain in the class was the right choice?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.187) “It’s because I deemed it to be the right choice that I had the resolve to keep her in the class, taking on the animosity from everyone else. This is getting redundant.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.187) “Ah, I see.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.187) “I don’t intend to give a poor apology. No matter how much I apologize, it’s a fact that I changed my opinion and judged that Kushida-san should remain in the class. It’s natural for you to resent me, and one day I may receive painful retaliation. However, I decided that the person who can become fighting strength for our class was Kushida. I have gradually become certain of that.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “Even if Kushida-san is an outstanding student, there are others who have no abilities. There was no need for it to be her.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “I won’t accept it. No matter how many people approve of you from here on out, I will never accept it.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.189) “I have no choice but to try hard so that you’ll approve of me then.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “I just said that I don’t approve of you.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.189) “The one responsibility for expelling Sakura-san lies with me. Yes, I won’t deny that. I can’t deny that. On the other hand, what should I do? Are you going to tell me from here on to quit school?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “Give Airi back.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.189) “… I can’t fulfill a request that can’t be done.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “That’s all I wish for. I don’t care what happens to the class.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.189) “The decision from that time was wrong.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.190) “If you’re dissatisfied, then perhaps you should have fought.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.190) “But that’s a pointless conversation. Even if you had fought, you had no means to resist us, after all.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.190) “I suppose so. Certainly, there’s not much that the likes of me could have done. Kiyopon used Airi’s feelings and cornered her without mercy. That kind of behavior is something that a normal person absolutely couldn’t have done.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.190) “Is Kushida-san really going to work for the sake of the class? She’s bound to betray you.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.190) “If Kushida-san drags us down moving forward, I’ll regret it.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.190) “However, even if I were to go to the past with my memories as I am now, what I would most likely do wouldn’t change much. I would repeat my decision to save Kushida-san and choose Airi to be expelled. If I were to make just one change, I wouldn’t have carelessly made a promise.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.190) “Why? Why Airi?”
[says] (p.190) “The issue is how we think about things. The events this time around have become a strong stimulus for the students whose names are lowest on the OAA. If they continue to fly low like this, then they may become the next ones to be expelled. Even just them possessing a stronger sense of danger can be thought of as a plus.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.191) “It’s as if we’re like Ryuuen’s class. Throwing away people without any abilities?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.191) “I wonder about that. I’m not sure what principles Ryueen goes by, but it’s a fact that it’s close to his reigning with fear in some sense. Our class policy up until now has been vague and too weak.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.191) “It kind of reminds me of when we started school. It’s the same as when we all acted on our own and had not a shred of cohesiveness.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.191) “The situation from that time was different. Preventing avoidable expulsions before they happen is important, but keeping those who we have to expel to a minimum was the issue at hand this time around.”
[says] (p.191) “It’s because Horikita felt the possibility of the benefits gained upon Kushida becoming an ally greatly outweighing Airi’s that she reached that conclusion. It’s also because I saw that future that I respected her opinion and threw her a lifeline.”
[says] (p.191) “Even though Airi disappeared, the class returned to their everyday lives before I knew it.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.191) “I understand your discontent, but did you think the same things when Yamauchi-kun was expelled?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.191) “He got what he deserved. It’s different this time around.”
[says] (p.192) “It’s the same. You’re just mad that one of your friends was sacrificed.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “What’s so wrong about that?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “I can’t accept that kind of reality. I can’t come to terms with it.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “Kushida-san indeed may have been a threat. She may now have a change of heart and work for the class from here on out. However, do you seriously think I’ll look at that and cooperate?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.192) “You have a point. When you were out for a whole week, it felt like you would become a long-term problem more so than anyone else.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.192) “However, you came to school. If you wanted to go out of your way to talk to me, you could’ve done so while continuing to stay absent. Isn’t that right?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “I still haven’t come up with an answer so I simply tried coming here.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.192) “An answer?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “I came to school to look for the answer I couldn’t find while holed up inside my room.”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.192) “What should I do to achieve revenge against Horikita-san and Kiyopon? I’m searching for that answer.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.193) “… You’re serious, aren’t you?”
[says:hasebe-haruka] (p.193) “I wanted to tell you today: I will make you regret expelling Airi.”
[says:ishigami-kyou] (p.193) “I don’t think either of you, Horikita or Haruka, are wrong. It might seem unfair, but those are my honest thoughts. At the end of the day, so long as I survive it’s alright, that’s at the core of it.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.193) “Everyone’s like that. It isn’t strange to want to save yourself.”
[says:ishigami-kyou] (p.193) “That’s why I can’t understand Haruka’s feelings just now. But despite that, I don’t think I have the right to tell her to stop. Even if it ends up causing trouble for the class.”
[says:ishigami-kyou] (p.193) “The group is half broken now. But still, I will be useful to the class as myself. While I might not do well in the Sports Festival, in turn I will study more and more to contribute to the class. If I don’t… I wouldn’t be able to rule out the possibility that I’ll get thrown out.”
[scene] (p.193) Haruka grabs a few strands of her own hair and pulls them out with all her might at “Give Airi back”; “The decision from that time was wrong.”; then leaves without drinking; Akito goes after her; jaw dropped; Keisei strikes the table with his fist before getting up. The coldest line yet: “I wanted to tell you today: I will make you regret expelling Airi.”
[rel:hasebe-haruka] (p.184–193) Haruka's revenge declaration — “I will make you regret expelling Airi.” — she grabs her own hair, leaves her drink, and walks out at 193.
[rel:horikita-suzune] (p.184–193) She stands her ground — the cafe confrontation; she won't cry, won't kneel; she acknowledges her responsibility but will not quit.
[rel:miyake-akito] (p.184–193) Akito listens in silence; he goes after Haruka when she leaves.
[rel:ishigami-kyou] (p.193) Keisei's honest confession — “I will study more and more to contribute to the class.”
[rel:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.185) “more than 500 points between us and Class A” — the gap she named.
[rel:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.191) She compares the class's policy to his “reigning with fear.”
[rel:yamauchi-haruki] (p.191) “did you think the same things when Yamauchi-kun was expelled?” — the Lucius precedent in the air.

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.199) “In order to defeat Sakayanagi-san’s class, I propose we form a cooperative relationship for the upcoming Sports Festival.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.199) “… What do you mean by cooperative relationship?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.199) “In this special exam, there are both mixed grade level and grade-specific aspects to the competition. I want to make the most of the system where if we win in a group competition with multiple people taking part, everyone will score equally.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.199) “Why our class? Would you mind if I ask your reasoning?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.199) “First of all, it goes without saying that Class A is out of the question. [says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.200) “So you’re saying you chose us by process of elimination, huh.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.200) “If it were through a simple process of elimination, I wouldn’t have teamed up with any class to begin with. Since the only person more untrustworthy than someone from Sakayanagi-san’s class is Ryuuen-kun, your class’s leader.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.200) “That’s true. Even I, now a fellow classmate, think so. There is no one I’d be more afraid of trusting my back to. That being the case, why did you propose a cooperative relationship that poses such a great risk to you?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.200) “To win, of course. We can’t advance without bringing an end to Class A’s overwhelming lead.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.200) “But it would be pointless if those hopes aren’t met, wouldn’t it? This guy will use any means available, that’s who he is. I know it well, since I have my own painful experiences. I can’t recommend it.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.200) “I didn’t intend to cut right to the chase during today’s discussion. I haven’t spoken to Ryuuen-kun like this for a while, and I just can’t trust someone who is so unabashedly late. However, when I saw you apologize for being late, Katsuragi-kun, I changed my mind. At the very least, I can trust you.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.200) “That’s very simplistic. Did you not consider that this attitude of mine may also be one of Ryuuen’s schemes?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.200) “If I’m not able to discern whether or not I can trust you, sooner or later, I’ll just be swallowed up, right?”

[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.201) “You seem a little different from before, Horikita. So I guess that means you’re growing, too, huh.”

[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.202) “But, to tell you the truth, I was of two minds on whether I should propose working together with your class to Ryuuen-kun.”

[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.204) “There’s plen’y of blind spots, and it doesn’t only need to be during the events.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.204) “You haven’t changed a bit. Certainly, the thought of that is terrifying, but… looks like we’re done here.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.210) “The enemy of my enemy is my friend. I’ll believe in that convenient saying our predecessors came up with,” Horikita replied.
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.210) “I don’t accept everything you’re saying, but one thing’s for sure—it ain’t a good idea to let Sakayanagi’s class keep running on ahead.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.211) “Even if you say that you’re gonna hold off a direct confrontation with her until the end of the school year, you can’t overturn the difference in class points with just that.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.211) “You’ve been listening in silence, but it’s about time you let us hear your opinion, Ayanokouji-kun.”
[says] (p.211) “Regarding the pros and cons, cooperation isn’t a bad idea. There may be some objections, but everyone understands that Sakayanagi is the target we need to take down. Yousuke and Kei will surely back you up here as well.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.211) “You want to move onto the contract, but not yet.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.211) “Not yet? Are you saying that you want to drag out more concessions?”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.211) “Let me confirm one last thing. Are you the one who came up with this proposal, Suzune? Or, was it Ayanokouji, the guy who’s calmly observing the situation? Which is it?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.211) “Will you not go along with it if it’s not from Ayanokouji? You and Ayanokouji-kun seem to have a relationship that you can’t let others hear about, after all.” Horikita replied in a way that left a lot between the lines.
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.211) “I can tell that the two of you have recognized each other as strong enemies —and the fact that I am out of place as well.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.211) “Did I say anything about that? I’m just telling you to answer who it is.”

[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.212) “… Why?”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.212) “Why, you ask? Well, dunno. Figure it out by yourself.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.212) “It would be better for both of us to have a proper contract in place, just to be sure. No, for your own sake in particular.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.212) “Of course we will. I intend to have Chabashira-sensei and Sakagami-sensei get involved in this as well.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.212) “Well then, I’ll leave the paperwork up to you, Horikita. Is that fine?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.212) “Yes. Would you perhaps let me bounce ideas off you for a bit, Katsuragi-kun?”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.212) “Alright then. After we’ve officially settled the contract, let’s take on the Sports Festival.”
[scene] (p.213–218) Katsuragi raises the Sakayanagi-participation problem — the numbers (37 vs 40); Ryuuen and Katsuragi bicker over the 90% / 70–80% / 95% estimates; the mock-Sakayanagi threat is rejected on ethics; AK interjects — he will make sure Sakayanagi does not participate, no points expected of him — Katsuragi, Horikita and Ryuuen are surprised; Ryuuen accepts AK’s proposal; “Katsuragi, get things dealt with on your end.” — “I’ll do that.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.213) “It’s great that we’ve finished our discussion regarding working together, but there’s now something that we must think about. One can easily think that Sakayanagi and Ichinose will join hands, so what do you plan to do about that?”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.213) “That ain’t a problem. Even if Sakayanagi and Ichinose worked together for this Sports Festival, we still have the advantage. [says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.213) “However, it’s Sakayanagi we’re talking about. She will have established a strategy to make up for her lack of people.”

[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “Have you grasped the rules? Sure, Sakayanagi can’t move her body to its fullest. [says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.214) “There ain’t no way that prideful Sakayanagi would show us a powerless, unsightly display.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “Things won’t line up so conveniently. We are given the right to resign from a competition. If she participates and then forfeits, then she can avoid … embarrassing herself.”

[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “Indeed, if things were normal, then she would pass on participating given her personality. [says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.214) “Maybe 90%.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “So from your unsubstantiated and carefree view it’s 90%? If that’s the case, then the actual value is even lower. I’d say 70-80% at best.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.214) “Be happy with that number.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “I can’t do that. If you want to talk certainty, then shoot for 95%.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.214) “Bullshit. But, if we want to be more certain, there’s a way. From now until the Sports Festival, we can thoroughly mock Sakayanagi. [says:horikita-suzune] (p.214) “From an ethical point of view, that’s unacceptable.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.214) “I agree. The school probably wouldn’t watch quietly either.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.215) “In the off chance Sakayanagi does show up, we’ll crush her completely.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.215) “It’s not that simple, don’t forget that we’re sinking to the bottom class.”
[says] (p.215) “Horikita. Are you factoring my contribution into our class’s victory?” I interjected.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.215) “For the most part, I’m not considering it. I’m leaving you, and only you, with a special status.”
[says] (p.215) “That’s good to hear. If whether or not Sakayanagi participates is threatening our cooperation, then I may be able to be of help.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.215) “What do you mean?”
[says] (p.216) “If you leave everything to me, I’ll make sure Sakayanagi doesn’t participate.”
[says] (p.216) “However, in exchange for making Sakayanagi not participate, I don’t want you to expect even a single point from me at the Sports Festival. That goes not just for Horikita, but you too, Ryuuen.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.216) “You haven’t been in my plans from the start. If you say you can hold back Sakayanagi, then that spares us some effort,” Ryuuen answered.
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.216) “I can’t even imagine what kind of plan you have, but if Horikita and Ryuuen believe in you, then I more or less don’t plan to say anything more than this on the matter. If Sakayanagi doesn’t participate, then pushing Class A to last place shouldn’t be that hard.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.216) “But can you really do it?”
[says] (p.216) “Yeah. There’s a high chance that she’ll sit out even if I don’t do anything, but you can leave it to me anyway. There’s a different matter I want to talk about, is that alright?”
[note] (p.216) “What is it?”, Horikita asked. — narrator names her as the speaker for that line.
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.217) “That’s an interesting idea, but…”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.217) “That certainly ain’t impossible going by the rules, but—”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.217) “Yeah, I’m not. Rejected.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.217) “You can deal with your personal feelings later. But frankly, it’s not a bad proposal. We might need to discuss the details, and check the rules again but—no, it’s Ayanokouji we’re talking about. You’ve probably proposed this after confirming the rules properly.”
[says] (p.217) “There’s no problem as far as rules go. Instead of our class going alone, we could cooperate with the students in Ryuuen’s class to lead to a more powerful outcome. Isn’t that right?” I asked Horikita.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.217) “Yes, that’s right. That would certainly…”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.217) “Accept it, Ryuuen. We should be advancing our preparations right now for a direct confrontation with Sakayanagi.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.217) “You hear me, Ayanokouji? After I crush Sakayanagi, you’re next.”
[says] (p.217) “If you’re making your way up, then that’ll be inevitable.”
[says:ryuuen-kakeru] (p.217) “Katsuragi, get things dealt with on your end.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.217) “I’ll do that.”
[says] (p.218) “Truly, a siege on Class A… huh.”
[says:katsuragi-kouhei] (p.218) “However, before that, making Sakayanagi not participate in the Sports Festival is top priority. For both our cooperation at the Sports Festival and Ayanokouji’s proposal, if we don’t clear that first step, then the ball can’t get rolling.”
[says] (p.218) “I understand. As for that, leave it to me.”

[says] (p.238) “I’ve got something important to say regarding the Sports Festival.”

### y2v6 p.302–317 — Ch.6: Sakayanagi comes to his room — the “special lesson” (AK POV)
[scene] (p.302–303) 11 AM festival day — cheers outside; “Director Sakayanagi’s hands”; the plan — keep her out via Director Sakayanagi's hint that the White Room people prevent contact; his room is prohibited; Ak never expected her to come — but she does: “Hello, Ayanokouji-kun.” — Sakayanagi at the door in casual clothes; she smiles.

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.303) “My apologies for bothering you.”

[says] (p.303) “I was just about to get started making it.”

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.304) “I bought this at the convenience store early this morning. It seems to be a new product, so I thought we might as well try it together.”

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.304) “Thank you for your consideration.”
[says] (p.304) “I don’t suppose you came here on a whim.”

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.304) “You really are a terrible person, Ayanokouji-kun. This was part of your strategy, wasn’t it?”
[says] (p.304) “Strategy? What do you mean?”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.304) “Fufu, you don’t need to play dumb, Ayanokouji-kun. You were almost sure —no, let me correct myself. You were sure I’d come here today, weren’t you?”
[scene] (p.305–307) She breaks down the plan — his supposed prediction; Director Sakayanagi's hint (White Room security); her being told so she'd skip the festival; instead she came to his room — exactly as he predicted; 11 AM — before noon; her own information network; the bodyguards — “It wasn’t just at this dorm, and they were stationed across the whole school, so it didn’t appear unnatural.”; “This was part of your strategy, wasn’t it?” — “This time, I paid 150 points to enjoy some time with Ayanokouji-kun.” — she pays 150 points in class points for this conversation; “The systems of this school are, to me, just an extension of playtime. [says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.305) “You wouldn’t know how it would play out if I were to participate.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.305) “You have a very high opinion of yourself, as usual.”

[says] (p.305) “It’s true that I’m sitting out the Sports Festival because Director Sakayanagi asked me to do so, but I never imagined he would tell his daughter about that.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.305) “How funny! Didn’t you ask him to tell me about this, Ayanokouji-kun?”

### y2v7 p.7–13 — Cultural festival rules; additional funds; midterm results
[scene] (p.7) Monday, November 1st; Chabashira opens the class with a review of the cultural festival rules and the announcement of additional funds.
[rule] (p.7) Each second-year class receives 5,000 private points per student for festival preparation (first-years 5,500; third-years 4,500); additional funds are granted for social contributions; unused allocations forfeit after the festival.
[rule] (p.8) Classes ranked 1st–4th receive 100 class points; 5th–8th receive 50; 9th–12th receive nothing.
[rule] (p.8) Additional funds breakdown for this class: Horikita 10,000 (student council member), Sudō 10,000 (club activity), Onodera 10,000 (club activity); Yōsuke received 3,000 for his club activity bonus, and Akito received 100; nine other students received hundreds to thousands.
[number] (p.8–9) This class's additional funds total 39,400 — the most among the second-year students (Sakayanagi's Class A 18,800; Ryūen's Class C 17,000; Ichinose's Class D 26,600).
[trivia] (p.9) Guests: 283 adults (10,000 pts each) + 202 minors (5,000 each) = 485 participants, 3,840,000 points in total; guests of honor include school-operation families and Keyaki Mall / convenience-store staff; homeroom teachers may not use points in their own grade.
[rule] (p.9) Homeroom teachers are restricted to using points in the grade for which they are responsible.
[rule] (p.10) Guests cannot exceed 10,000 points in pocket money; a cell-phone app monitors sales in real time; the app is disabled at 4 pm when the festival ends.
[says:ike-kanji] (p.10) “Is it possible to use more than 10,000 points in pocket money?” — Ike's preemptive question.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.10) “If the sales are the same amount, what would the ranking be? I know this is very extreme, but what happens if all classes receive the same amount of 320,000 points and are side by side?” — Horikita asks about a full 12-class tie.
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.10) “If the sales are equal, they are treated as the same rank. If all 12 classes make equal sales, as Horikita says, then all classes get 100 class points as first place.” — Chabashira answers.
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.10–11) “However, the total amount of sales can only be confirmed after the exam, and any manipulation of sales by third parties is not allowed. It is impossible for the classes to discuss and make a plan to combine sales before the festival, or to …  make an arrangement to divide the sales equally after the festival is over.” — no-collusion rule.
[says:maezono] (p.11) “I don't think an equal number of sales among the classes would be normal. I don't think you need to worry about it.” — Maezono voices her doubts; Horikita had a point.
[number] (p.11–12) Second-semester midterm results: Keisei took first place (perfect score in all subjects); Horikita second, 3 points behind; Sudō 11th with 367 (73 Modern Japanese, 76 Chemistry, 70 Social Studies, 78 Mathematics, 70 English); honor roll: Yōsuke, Kushida, Matsushita, Wang; Ayanokōji 14th (perfect Mathematics only).
[note] (p.12) Sudō's OAA: academic ability C+, physical ability A+, adaptability C, social contribution D — “a well-known fact that Sudō was working hard on his studies”; Ayanokōji's own 14th place was deliberate (he did not want to startle the class).
[note] (p.13) The narration ties Sudō's motivation to his love for Horikita, who taught him how to study, and notes that the expulsion of Sakura Airi pushed the lower-ranked students to work even harder.
### y2v7 p.13–16 — Maid café planners; stall-location inspection; Satō's distance
[scene] (p.13) The six maid café planners (Satō, Matsushita, Mii-chan [Wang], Maezono, Horikita, Ayanokōji) meet after school; the outdoor option is crossed out; the café location (the classroom) is fixed; stall location undecided; meetings move to cell phones to prevent leaks.
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.13) “Hasebe-san and Miyake-kun, what will you do about them?” — Matsushita asks about Haruka and Akito.
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.14) “They come to school every day, but they don't want to talk to anyone. It means they keep antagonizing us, the whole class.”
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.14) “I think Hasebe-san is going to try to do something to the class in the future.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.14) “There's very little we can do in advance … … Preaching to them to stop taking revenge will only get on their nerves.” — Horikita, looking off into the distance; she adds “If she's really looking for an opportunity for revenge, she certainly won't put it off for months.”
[note] (p.14) The “Just what?” between those two statements prints untagged; not assigned.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.14) “I've heard from Ayanokōji-kun that Hasebe-san has no intention of working as a maid. [says:wang-mei-yu] (p.15) “It's a lot farther than I thought it would be.” — Mii-chan's first impression of the special building's third floor.
[says:satou-maya] (p.15) “Oh, um. I was thinking... yeah, I guess I think it's a little far away too.” — Satō, distracted.
[says:maezono] (p.16) “I guess the second floor is better than the third floor! More to the point, the first floor would be ideal,” — Maezono mutters.
[says:wang-mei-yu] (p.16) “But we should make a decision soon. It's getting pretty full.” — Mii-chan makes a sour face at her phone.
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.16) “That's right. Two of the five places we picked up are now occupied... However, there are still candidates from the first to the third floor, which I'd say is a bit of a problem.”
[note] (p.16–17) Satō is off all day; Matsushita suspects she “wants to talk but can't … … keeps things inside”; Ayanokōji does not know why; the “Satō whisperer” speculation is Matsushita's, unconfirmed.
### y2v7 p.17–22 — Sakayanagi scouts the special building; the Ryūen cooperation leak
[scene] (p.17) Hashimoto (Class A) calls out to the group outside the second floor; Sakayanagi and Kamuro arrive with him; they, too, are scouting stall locations; Hashimoto needles Horikita about teaming with Ryūen.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.17) “Yo, Ayanokōji. Are you also looking for a place to open a stand for the festival?”
[says] (p.17) “Well, I’m not sure. They may have already decided, or they may not have even decided whether to go indoors or outdoors.” — the evasive answer.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.17) “No decision? That's an obvious lie. Are you telling me that you're taking Horikita all the way out to the special building to roam around for no reason? Please tell me what kind of show you're going to put on.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.17–18) “Then you mean he's simply enjoying his harem?” — he points out Ayanokōji is the only male of the six and asks Kamuro to agree.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.17) “You must be similar, Hashimoto-kun. Sakayanagi-san and Kamuro-san. You are the only boy, even if the number of people is different. I wonder if it's because you're aware of that that you're making strange comments?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “Satō, you've been spending a lot of time with people like Matsushita, Wang and Maezono.”
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.18) “Don't try to get anything out of us.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “I didn't mean it like that. It's just...”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “Oops, any more than that would be superfluous?” — grinning, looking at Sakayanagi
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.18) “You appear to want to say something, Hashimoto-kun.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “I'm worried about your class, my friend. It seems that you have teamed up with... Ryūen for the sports festival, but do you think you can trust him forever?” — his pointed question to Horikita.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “I just thought you were going to team up with Ryūen again. If you are going to team up with him, be careful,” — he says, as if he had the heart of an old woman.
[says:matsushita-chiaki] (p.18) “We're in a hurry, and I don't think we can play word games forever, you know? Everyone?”
[says:kamuro-masumi] (p.18) “She doesn't like you, does she?” — playing with the bad atmosphere.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.18) “Maybe. I'm just asking for some reasoning... Anyways, good luck with that.”
[says:wang-mei-yu] (p.18) “That was a little scary...” — Mii-chan, relieved, pats her chest, murmuring to Satō.
[says:satou-maya] (p.18) “Huh? Oh, um, yeah. A little bit.”
[note] (p.19) Sakayanagi said nothing and went into the class they had watched earlier.
[note] (p.19) “A sports festival is a sports festival, a cultural festival is a cultural festival…” prints untagged; Sakayanagi's class is one enemy to be defeated alongside Ryūen's.
[note] (p.19) “It's a certainty that we'll cooperate with Ryūen-kun's class in the upcoming cultural festival, right?” and “Yes. When we cooperated with each other at the sports festival, we also talked about working together during the cultural festival.” both print untagged; Horikita and Ayanokōji are the two who know the deal; not assigned.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.19) “It's true that it's difficult to trust Ryūen-kun personally. That's why I put Katsuragi-kun in between the two of us. I'm sure It'll be fine.” — Horikita, per the adjacent narration "Horikita explained to them".
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.19) “The ones who know are myself and Ayanokōji-kun. Then there are the four of you who started the maid café. In Ryūen's class, there's Katsuragi. He may have told other important classmates, but I don't see the benefit of leaking it.” — Horikita, same adjacent narration.
[note] (p.19–20) “I didn't care so much about it during the sports festival because it went well, but when they said something like that, I couldn't help but feel uneasy... Are you sure you're okay with trusting them?” — printed untagged; Maezono or Mii-chan voiced the unease; not assigned.
[note] (p.19–20) “Yes, I felt it too. Even if he doesn't betray you, isn't it conceivable that the cooperation was leaked?” — printed untagged; not assigned.
[rule] (p.20) Stall-floor vote by rock-paper-scissors: four rocks (first floor), two papers (AK and Matsushita), zero scissors (third floor); first floor (50,000 pts) wins; Horikita applies for it by phone immediately.
[note] (p.20) “So, are we done for the day?” — printed untagged; not assigned. “No, I have something to tell you first.” — Ayanokōji's line (his gathering of maid café intel).
[says] (p.20) “I don't think there won't be any female customers, but in terms of ratio, there'll be a considerable difference.”
[note] (p.21) “I heard that there are butler cafés in the world, the opposite of maid cafés. The butler isn't a girl, but a dressed up man.” prints untagged; the listeners had not heard of butler cafés; not assigned.
[note] (p.21) “You know a lot too, Horikita.” — aimed at Horikita, speaker untagged; not assigned.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.21) “I'll at least gather information. You can decide if it's useful or not after you learn it.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.21) “Floors, walls, ceilings, and other chairs also vary a bit in damage due to age. I'd like you to check that as well so that you don't miss anything.” — Horikita assigns the floor check.
[says] (p.21) “And also about the uniforms, we shouldn't push the eroticism too blatantly.” — prompts Horikita's shocked "Eh?! What did you say?"
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.21) “Eh?! What did you say?” — Horikita, shocked.
[says] (p.21) “Eroticism. Eros and eroticism have been seen as important elements in art since ancient times. Showing underwear and the like is out of the question, but it's important, however, not to refuse the hope that it might be visible.”
[says] (p.21) “Since I'm in charge of running the maid café, of course I can't cut corners. I studied to be as helpful as possible.”
[says] (p.22) “I also thought about a sales strategy. In addition to providing food and drinks, we'll sell the right to take pictures, called Cheki.”
[says] (p.22) “Using a specialized camera, the price would be 800 points for a photo of one maid. For a photo session with a customer, the price would be 1,200 points. In order to reduce costs, I suggested using a printer to print out the photos after taking them with a cell phone, but the Professor, who taught me this, rejected the idea. He said, ‘If you neglect quality for the sake of profit, no one will pay attention to you.’”
[says] (p.22) “No, I'm bullish on the film. We have a plan to sell out. The condition, of course, is that we don't release the photos. Also, under Horikita's leadership, the boys have begun setting up a food stall, but the food here should also be linked to the maid café.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.22) “The competition for restaurants will inevitably be high as there are signs of multiple booths, including the other grades. So we'll specialize in snacks while keeping our prices low.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.22) “It's essential we use it as a stepping stone to our main goal, the maid café. We can reduce the price of the tickets for one drink, which can then be used at the maid café for those who purchased said ticket.”
[trait] (p.19–22) He reveals the Ryūen cooperation to the four planners (only they plus Katsuragi knew); argues maid-café economics (male customers as the main target; photo tickets at 800/1,200 pts; film sellout planned; no releasing photos); Horikita is surprised by his knowledge; he keeps the cooperation secret beyond these five.
[rel:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.17–18) She watches the exchange with a wry smile; says nothing; goes into the class they had been watching.
[rel:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.17–18) He probes the Ryūen alliance (“do you think you can trust him forever?”); smiles thinly at Ayanokōji later when the leak goes public (p.30).
[rel:kamuro-masumi] (p.17–18) Is with Sakayanagi and Hashimoto; needles at Hashimoto (“She doesn't like you, does she?”).
[rel:horikita-suzune] (p.19–22) He informs her of the detailed plan; male-customer targeting; Cheki pricing; she applies for the first floor.
### y2v7 p.23–26 — Keyaki Mall: Sudō's growth; Akito and Haruka; Kei's morning
[scene] (p.23) §2 Keyaki Mall — Ayanokōji goes alone for a price survey; finds Sudō at a building map; Keyaki Mall in late November.
[says] (p.23) “You were the center of attention today, Sudō.”

[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “Haha, no doubt. I think my past self would be yelling like, ‘What the hell? What's the use of studying and memorizing words and formulas? You should practice basketball more instead of wasting your time like that!’”

[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “Huh? Well...”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “You can't even remember simple formulas, what are you?” — formed after a moment's thought.
[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “I'm going to become a professional basketball player, so it doesn't matter,”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “Ugh, fine! What's the right response in that case? Isn't a professional with brains one step ahead of you? It's a little tricky when you can't reason with.” — Sudō laughs bitterly as he racks his brains.
[says:sudou-ken] (p.23) “To be honest, I'm getting impatient since it's getting a little more difficult to understand. Up until now, once I got the hang of it, it went pretty smoothly...”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “I had to take some time off today.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “Lately, my eyesight's been deteriorating to the point where I'm aware of it.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “I've always had a clear vision since I was a little kid, but lately it's been strange.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “I'm looking for an optician to measure my eyesight. I've never been to one before, and I was wondering where it was.”
[says] (p.24) “So you've been staring at a guide map. If you're feeling a strong sense that your eyesight is declining, there's a good chance that your eyesight is actually deteriorating.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “Even if my eyesight is going to be failing in the future, I'm going to keep studying, man. I mean, I'm dying for basketball and I'm not going to stop. But, while I dream of becoming a pro, I'm starting to think that I might have other options.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “Don't laugh, okay?”
[says] (p.24) “I won't.”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.24) “I thought I could go to a normal university and continue my studies, and even if I could force my way into the pros because of my academics, there's no way they'd use me in the sports world if I'm not good enough. [says:sudou-ken] (p.25) “Yeah, that's right.”

[note] (p.25) “Ah.” — Sudō's startled noticing Akito and Haruka's backs; “It's not a date, is it?” and “I guess not.” both print untagged — one of them is Ayanokōji's question about the two; speaker order not assigned.
